label: YS-29
title: NatSpec dead-letter reference to KNOWN_WITHDRAWERS: comment promises automated withdrawer revocation loop that does not exist, leaving a stale SYA authorization on decommissioned strategies
description: The contract-level NatSpec at lines 22-26 states: 'Other withdrawers, if any, are revoked here too when known (see KNOWN_WITHDRAWERS).' No KNOWN_WITHDRAWERS constant or enumeration loop exists anywhere in the file. Historical grants from ReplaceSYAMainnet.s.sol called setWithdrawer(newSYA, true) on the old strategies, leaving the live SYA (0x3bBE9283...) as an authorized withdrawer on both YS_DOLA_OLD and YS_USDC_OLD after decommissioning. The inline implementation comment at lines 123-124 accurately acknowledges the gap: 'other withdrawers, if any, must be revoked by the operator if they appear — there is no on-chain enumeration of withdrawers.' These two comments are mutually contradictory. Operational severity is Low: skimSurplus is gated whenNotPaused, so the residual SYA withdrawer authorization on the paused strategies is completely inert. However, the misleading NatSpec could cause a future operator to believe the revocation was automated, potentially leaving stale authorizations if the strategies are ever unpaused.
impact: No immediate token risk (skimSurplus is blocked by the whenNotPaused gate applied in _decommission step 4). If the strategies are ever unpaused for emergency residual recovery, the stale SYA withdrawer authorization would permit the live SYA to call skimSurplus on the decommissioned strategies — routing yield from any residual to the SYA's configured recipient rather than the treasury. This is a latent authorization footgun.
recommendation: Remove the '(see KNOWN_WITHDRAWERS)' reference from the NatSpec or add an explicit setWithdrawer(LIVE_SYA_ADDRESS, false) call for the known live SYA address (0x3bBE9283...) in _decommission, with a corresponding post-assert require(!s.authorizedWithdrawers(LIVE_SYA_ADDRESS)). The inline comment at lines 123-124 is accurate and should be made consistent with the NatSpec.
